::: {#def-homogeneous-network-interference .theorem}
## Homogeneous network interference

An exposure mapping is [separable](#def-separability) and all its component functions are [network exposure mappings](#def-network-exposure-mapping) with respect to a graph set $\mathcal H$. An NPSEM satisfies homogeneous network interference if all its exposure mappings do.

The name is the decomposition. *Interference* arrives through separable summaries; it is *homogeneous* because those summaries treat every node alike ([positional invariance](#def-positional-invariance)) and take finitely many levels ([boundedness](#def-boundedness)). When $\mathcal H$ holds [graph generators](#def-graph-generator) rather than fixed graphs, the same assumption is called [homogeneous random network interference](#def-homogenous-random-network-interference).
:::
